posts.title: Penny Flanagan Becomes First Native American Woman Elected as Senator, DFL Strikes Big in Minnesota
posts.excerpt: Penny Flanagan becomes the first Native American woman elected to the United States Senate, and the DFL completes a trifecta for the 2nd time in 4 years in Minnesota's state legislature.
posts.body:
## **Minnesota Continues Blue, About Penny**

Minnesota Lieutenant Governor Penny Flanagan has officially been elected Senator of Minnesota, replacing retiring Senator Tina Smith and defeating Republican Nominee Michelle Tafoya. She helps with the new Democratic Senate Majority, winning 53.7% of the vote to Tafoya’s 43.6%

Penny Flanagan, a Native American from St. Louis Park, Minnesota, began her career working in former Senator Paul Wellstone’s Campaign as an organizer for the Native American community. Her early career focused on getting the Native American vote out, organizing in Native American populations, and pushing legislation and awareness around the Native American community in Minnesota.

She began her political career on the Board for Minneapolis Public Schools after being elected in 2004 and served from 2005 to 2009. She then ran for the Minnesota State House of Representatives but dropped out due to her mother facing health issues. After a couple of years of different jobs, she ran unopposed for Minnesota State House of Representatives in a 2015 special election and won re-election in 2016. In 2018, she ran with Governor Tim Walz as his Lieutenant Governor and was re-elected in 2022.

## **News Around Minnesota**

The Minnesota Democratic Farmer-Labor (DFL) Party struck big not only in the Senate race, but also down the ballot. United States Senator Amy Klobuchar won her bid for Governor, succeeding Tim Walz, against Republican Nominee and Minnesota State House Speaker Lisa Demuth with 55.5% of the vote. Amy Klobuchar has been serving as Minnesota’s Senator since 2007 and has been touted as one of the most bipartisan members of Congress. She also ran for President in the 2016 Presidential Election.

The DFL also flipped the Minnesota House of Representatives, completing a trifecta for the 2nd time in four years as they held onto the majority in the State Senate. In Minnesota’s State House of Representatives, Zack Randolph has been elected as the Speaker Designate for the 2027 Legislative Session, succeeding Melissa Hortman, who was tragically assassinated just last year. Erin Murphy is re-elected as the Senate Majority Leader and looks to continue the work from 2024.

Governor Tim Walz shared that he hopes to return back to teaching as he leaves the Governor’s Office in January. Tim Walz was a United States House Representative for the highly competitive 1st Congressional District in Minnesota in 2007 before running for Governor in 2018. 2024 Democratic Presidential Nominee Kamala Harris chose Tim Walz to be her running mate, in which they lost to President Donald Trump and Vice Presidential nominee J.D. Vance in the general election.

## **What this means for the United States Senate**

In order to achieve a majority, the Democratic Party needed to retain all Senate seats and flip  four additional seats. Not only did they complete that, but they also flipped 3 additional seats on top of that, with 2 states yet to finish counting votes. The Democratic Party currently has a 54-44 Senate Majority, but with Alaska and Mississippi, they could bring that number up to 56.

In the House of Representatives, the Democratic Party has flipped 43 seats, obtaining a confirmed 252 seat majority. 218 is the number to beat for a simple majority in the House of Representatives, which Democrats have cleared easily. NBC News projects that Democrats could win up to 7 more Congressional seats once all votes have been tallied, reaching up to 50 seats that have been flipped.

Penny Flanagan, among other newly-elected Senators, have already called for Chuck Schumer to step down as Senate Majority Leader, citing that “it is time for new leadership” at a “point of a new movement.” Growing frustrations from both chambers and around the country have been expressed as voters don’t think Chuck Schumer, nor Hakeem Jeffries, are up for the fight against Donald Trump and continuing this blue wave that the Democrats are currently riding on. In other news, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a prominent figure in the progressive movement, has actually endorsed Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker of the House. She went live on Instagram to explain the process of voting for speaker as her base is disappointed in her for the decision.
